reason:
This is an error stop at Code-Bouncer (history length 5), so I have no repair verbs.
It is the second failure from the same cause.
The first stop was `fork/exec /usr/bin/git: resource temporarily unavailable` (EAGAIN) at 10:41:19.
The tackler judged the cause cleared and resumed.
The re-launch then failed 22 seconds later at bootstrap with `run list-commands: exit status 1`, which is the reed tmux version probe failing to start.
The run state itself is clean: that step was refused before it changed anything (status_moved false), and status.json shows Darn-Write done and Code-Bouncer failed.
The tackler read the wrong limit.
It checked `ulimit -u` (113180), but the limit that binds is the systemd user slice cgroup.
/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice has pids.max 3000, and pids.events reads `max 3207`, so that cap has refused a task 3207 times.
At 10:42 the slice held about 2600 of its 3000 tasks.
That load is several concurrent loom drives and steps across the LYMHUB and lym-csharp hubs, three or four `lym gate test` runs, a dotnet test with MSBuild nodes, Chrome and VS Code.
So the cause has not cleared.
It recurs whenever a gate or build burst takes up the remaining ~400 tasks, and a third plain re-launch would race the same cap.
The fix is a host change (raise the slice's TasksMax) or less concurrency, and neither belongs to this run.
question:
Run review-setup-audit stopped twice at Code-Bouncer with fork EAGAIN.
The cause is the user-1000.slice cgroup task cap (pids.max 3000, already hit 3207 times, about 2600 in use at 10:42), not the run.
Should the operator raise the cap, for example `sudo systemctl set-property user-1000.slice TasksMax=8192`, or should concurrent runs and gate tests be cut back before this run is re-launched?
The run's state is clean, so once there is headroom a plain re-launch of the Code-Bouncer row, with no goto, should settle it.
